weapons.name: Molotov Cocktail
weapons.intro: A rather primitive weapon capable of dealing massive damage to certain types of enemies. A handmade gasoline firebomb, named after Vyacheslav Molotov of the Soviet Union during World War II. You can create these by combining an Empty Bottle with a Gas Tank . They are particularly useful against enemies that are sensitive to fire, such as leeches.

He was assumed dead, but the T-Virus brought him back as a Zombie just like all the other poor souls on the train. Due to his resilient body protection, he is a more difficult zombie to put to rest.

enemies.name: Plague Crawler

enemies.name: Bat

They are not worth dealing with, as your main concern will be the giant one attacking you. As soon as you kill the Giant Bat , these pests will simply disappear.

Its time in isolation obviously caused it to undergo further mutation, as this monster is much stronger than its counterparts, and can sustain a lot more damage before it is well and truly dead.

enemies.intro: (Resident Evil Remake) Cerberus, essentially a doberman infected with the T-Virus, is a fairly common enemy in the game. enemies.name: Forest Speyer
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil Remake) Forest Speyer , once a proud member of Bravo Team, is now one of the living dead. Based on his injuries, he was pecked to death by Crows infected with the T-Virus. Shortly after finding his body he will spring to life and come after you. This terrible demon is one of the first boss fights you encounter in the game, and it takes a large amount of ammunition to scare it away. You can read all about it in the Family Picture & Notes file, which describes the architect of the mansion George Trevor, his wife Jessica and their daughter Lisa being held prisoner by Umbrella and being experimented on with the T-Virus. enemies.name: Adder
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil Remake) Small in comparison to the one you encounter earlier on, these pests are poisonous, and can hinder your progress when the need for a Blue Herb arises. Although small, these should be avoided. Since you only encounter them a few times during the game, you shouldn't bother wasting any ammunition on these.

enemies.name: Wasp
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil Remake) An ordinary wasp that has been infected with the T-Virus and subsequently grown to roughly four times its original size. These insects are now more deadly than ever, being able to deliver a much more potent poison with its stinger. If you ever find yourself in a swarm, don't waste any ammunition on them, just run like hell.

enemies.name: Neptune
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil Remake) Neptune is the code name for an experiment involving administering the T-Virus to an ordinary Great White shark. The result is a much larger, much more ferocious predator. enemies.name: Plant 42
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil Remake) This huge monstrous bulb is the product of the researchers in the Guardhouse Residence experimenting with the T-Virus on plants. The result of which is a carnivorous plant that feeds on the blood of its victims. It is said that this plant grew this large by feeding off the contaminated water from the broken water tank in the basement.

enemies.name: Hunter
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil Remake) An extremely powerful creature with claws on all four limbs, and the ability to jump several metres in the air. enemies.name: Vines

There are several ways to get rid of these: Ignite the flammable fluid surrounding the vent area with your Lighter . As Leon, use the Flamethrower . These plants act similar to the Ivy , but with the addition that its acid spits now have the ability to poison you, making them far more dangerous.

enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 2) A giant larvae of the Giant Moth . These little creatures pose little threat to you. There's only one instance of where you have to kill them, and that's to access the computer in the Computer Room .

This insect is certainly more of a pest than a threat as it tries to attack you with its oversized body. The Enhanced Shotgun or the Grenade Launcher are the best weapons to use in this fight. Only a few blasts from each is enough to dispose of this bothersome creature.

enemies.name: Zombie
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 2 Remake) The most common enemy in the game. These zombies are the poor police officers and residents of Raccoon City after being infected by the T-Virus. Now they are shambling corpses, roaming the hallways and streets, ready to devour anything living they come across.

enemies.name: Licker
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 2 Remake) These aggressive creatures are the result of bio-weapon research conducted using the T-Virus. They are capable of climbing on walls and ceilings using their immensely large and powerful claws. Their weakness is their inability to see, however their hearing has developed to be incredibly sensitive.

enemies.name: Zombie Dog
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 2 Remake) These canines have been infected with the T-Virus, resulting in them becoming zombified. This has not restricted their ability to move incredibly fast and agile, and they will pursue you relentlessly. They do not take much ammunition to put down, but their speed can make them difficult to target.

enemies.name: Tyrant
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 2 Remake) This monstrous stranger will pursue you throughout the Police Station, and attempt to punch you to death should you come within striking distance. enemies.name: Alligator
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 2 Remake) An alligator that has mutated and grown to immense proportions due to the effects of the T-Virus. This lives underneath Raccoon City and you encounter it whilst playing as Leon as you traverse the sewers in search of the entrance to the NEST facility. The sequence in which you encounter it involves you having to avoid its bites. This

enemies.name: G-Adult
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 2 Remake) These monstrous mutations are the result of the failed offspring produced by the creature known as "G" . They start off as G-Young , but grow into these within a short space of time. These adults can crawl and swim through the sewage systems of Raccoon City very quickly. If they manage to grab you, they can infect you with a toxin th

enemies.name: G-Young
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 2 Remake) These monstrous mutations are the result of the failed offspring produced by the creature known as "G" . They start off as this infant version of themselves, but grow into a large G-Adult within a short space of time. Despite being much smaller than their eventual adult counterpart, they are still a dangerous enemy that should be dis

enemies.name: Ivy
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 2 Remake) These walking abominations are actually the poor scientists of the Underground Laboratory that have been infected by Plant 43, a mutant plant experiment that spread itself throughout the facility. enemies.name: G (First Form)
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 2 Remake) This creature is the result of a human being directly injected with the G-Virus. The human in question is none other than William Birkin, the creator of the G-Virus, who only subjected himself to his own creation in an effort to take back what was stolen from him. The G-Virus causes uncontrollable mutation, first targeting the arm th

enemies.name: G (Second Form)
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 2 Remake) This is the secondary mutation of the G-Virus infected William Birkin. Damage sustained to a creature infected with the G-Virus triggers a surge of uncontrolled mutations. Despite being in the early stages of mutation, practically all recognisable features of the former human have been lost, even the host's head has been replaced, wi

enemies.name: G (Third Form)
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 2 Remake) This is the third mutation of the G-Virus infected William Birkin. Damage sustained to a creature infected with the G-Virus triggers a surge of uncontrolled mutations. All traces of the former human have been lost now, leaving a completely alien-looking monster with two additional arms. This is the purest form of this creature.

enemies.name: G (Fourth Form)
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 2 Remake) This is the fourth mutation of the G-Virus infected William Birkin. Damage sustained to a creature infected with the G-Virus triggers a surge of uncontrolled mutations. enemies.name: G (Fifth Form)
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 2 Remake) This is the final mutation of the G-Virus infected William Birkin. The sheer bulk of this creature is its downfall, with the mutation of itself completely out of control as it desperately tries to cling onto its own life in order to destroy all others.

In fact, the best way to avoid them is to equip your lighter, the light will result in the bats staying away from you.

Her first mutation removes her human appearance and trades it for a green-skinned humanoid with increased str

The big difference between this and her second form is her incredible durability, which allows her to shrug off attacks from any weapon other than the Linear Launcher .

enemies.name: Ooze
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil Revelations) Regular Oozes are mutated humans who have been exposed to the T-Abyss Virus. Ooze dynamically change the structure of their bodies, which allows them to hide in vents, creep through floor grates, and surprise agents with attacks from unsuspecting places. Their weak point is their head.

enemies.name: Tricorne Ooze
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil Revelations) The Tricorne Ooze (or Shooter Ooze as it is commonly aliased) is a variant of the regular Ooze . They prefer to fight from long range and have a sharp gun-like appendage that shoots spinning bone projectiles at the player. enemies.name: Pincer Ooze
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil Revelations) The Pincer Ooze is a variant of the regular Ooze . They have over-sized arms that are covered in huge spikes, and they have a surprisingly long reach so it is best to fight these creatures from a distance. As with the regular Oozes, their weak spot is also their head.

enemies.name: Chunk Ooze
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil Revelations) The Chunk Ooze (or Exploding Ooze) is another variant of the regular Ooze . This type has undergone a horrible mutation and turned into flesh bags filled with explosive gas. These Oozes tend to guard doorways and hide around corners. enemies.intro: (Resident Evil Revelations) The Globster is a mysterious B.O.W.s that appears to be some sort of aquatic animal horrifically transformed by the T-Abyss Virus. You encounter these both on land and in the sea. Be sure to avoid them completely when they are in water, as they are capable of swallowing you whole. enemies.name: Fenrir
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil Revelations) Fenrir are wild wolves that have been exposed to the T-Abyss Virus. They usually travel in packs, which means you'll usually have to fight off a multitude of these, and they like to attack from all directions. Their weak spot is their exposed ribcage on the side of their bodies.

enemies.name: Black Fenrir
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil Revelations) The Black Fenrir is a larger variant of the regular Fenrir . You will usually find at least one of these in every pack of Fenrir you encounter, almost like an alpha-male role. They take more firepower to take down, but their exposed ribcage is still their weakness like their smaller counterparts.

enemies.name: Hunter
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil Revelations) Hunters are large, fast-moving B.O.W. creatures that were originally created by the Umbrella corporation. Their design has been improved and are now able to be transported to the weapon of a terrorist attack. It was these creatures that were used as part of the attack on Terragrigia.

enemies.name: Farfarello
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil Revelations) Farfarello are advanced Hunters that have the ability to cloak. These creatures jump in and out of invisibility and are less aggressive than regular Hunters. They prefer to sneak up on you rather than charging full-bore.

enemies.name: Wall Blister
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil Revelations) Wall Blisters are horrifying snail-like creatures that hibernate by sticking to walls and ceilings and hide within their invulnerable shells. When Wall Blisters are dormant, nothing can disturb them. When they wake, however, they immediately charge you with their giant tentacles flailing.

enemies.name: Ghiozzo
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil Revelations) Ghiozzo are goldfish modified by the T-Abyss Virus. They don't resemble their original forms and instead look like spiky piranhas. They are deadly both in and out of the water, and are fast moving that makes them difficult to target. On land they launch themselves up at you and attack with their razor sharp teeth.

enemies.name: Sea Creeper
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil Revelations) These horrifying creatures are the mermaids of your worst nightmares. Their chest areas are completely composed of teeth, and they will attempt to latch on and digest anyone who comes too close.

enemies.name: Malacoda
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil Revelations) These repulsive tentacles inhabit the ocean and always attack in groups. They move very fast through the water and have the ability to attack with both blunt force and with airborne explosive B.O.W. sacks. Malacoda are parasitic, and Veltro has spread rumours that they have been effectively used to create aquatic super-organisms.

enemies.name: Scagdead
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil Revelations) These creatures are the result of further mutation to someone infected with the T-Abyss Virus. They are large, malformed monsters that have an organic saw-like appendage on one arm, capable of dealing an instant-death attack.

enemies.name: Rachael Ooze
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil Revelations) This is the result of Rachael being reanimated by the T-Abyss Virus. She is much stronger than a regular Ooze , and is capable of moving at fast speed.

enemies.name: Draghignazzo
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil Revelations) This large B.O.W. is assumed to be the product of combing the T-Abyss Virus with a shellfish. Because of this, this creature has an extremely tough outer shell that can deflect almost anything you fire at it. enemies.name: Scarmiglione
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil Revelations) This B.O.W. is the product of combining the T-Abyss Virus with DNA of a species of shark. The result is a terrifying monster that has razor sharp claws and an extremely tough exterior that can withstand most forms of weaponry. enemies.name: Norman Mutant
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil Revelations) This monster is the result of the leader of the Veltro Jack Norman injecting himself with an overdose of the T-Abyss Virus. This causes him to mutate into a creature nicknamed "The Ultimate Abyss", and provides him with abilities unseen in any other T-Abyss monster so far. They are extremely resilient, however, and the threat they pose is increased exponentially by the chainsaw they wield. No target, no matter how strong, can survive even a single hit from these warriors.

The Majini who wear red shirts take a leader role among them, and have a higher endurance than usual.

enemies.name: J'avo
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 6) J'avo are mutated soldiers that carry a variety of weapons and are found, often in groups, throughout China, Edonia, and inside Neo Umbrella facilities donning special military armour. J'avo have been mutated by the C-Virus, which makes them difficult to kill and capable of surviving multiple shots to the head.

enemies.name: Chrysalid
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 6) After a J'avo is defeated, it will occasionally transform into a hard cocoon. If left alone, the cocoon will hatch into an advanced J'avo - a Strelat , Napad , Meset or Gnezdo ! It is possible to destroy a chrysalid before it hatches, but due to their tough exterior it may take a lot of ammunition to do so.

enemies.name: Strelat
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 6) This B.O.W. looks and moves like a lizard and generally appears after a J'avo has turned into a chrysalid cocoon. Strelats tend to attack from long range with needles that it emits from the fins around its neck. These projections move fast, but it's easy to see them coming - it emits steam from the fins around its neck before firing. To kee

enemies.name: Meset
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 6) This rare B.O.W. has a bird-like appearance and behaviour. The Mesets typically avoids confrontation by flying around your position and eventually diving in to attack.The attack cannot be countered, so you need to shoot it down before it gets a chance to attack.

enemies.name: Napad
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 6) The Napad is a heavily armoured B.O.W. that is seemingly indestructible. Its attacks are straightforward - it charges at you or punches you, both of which can be countered or easily avoided by staying out of its way. If the Napad connects with a punch, it grabs you and slams you to the ground if you don't manage to break free. Put simply, s

enemies.name: Gnezdo
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 6) This unique B.O.W. appears as a swarm of insects shaped like a human, but its true form is that of a large, bee-like insect. In battle, it hides within the swarm and only emerges when the swarm is dispersed after suffering a certain amount of damage.

enemies.name: Lepotitsa
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 6) This bulbous beast carries gas inside that can turn humans into zombies . If there are other humans nearby, it will navigate towards them and spew its blue gas onto them, transforming them into zombies. Shooting this creature in its body will cause it to spew grey gas, which causes damage at close range.

enemies.name: Iluzija
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 6) This giant snake B.O.W. has optic camouflage that makes it very difficult to see. However, dispatching this monster is fairly easy since it has only one attack that is very easy avoid. This Iluzija rears its head back, opening its mouth, and thus giving away its position before it charges at you.

enemies.name: Rasklapanje
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 6) This grotesque B.O.W. has a humanoid shape but can barely walk. Its only attack is to clumsily grab at you or your partner. If a Rasklapanje makes contact with you, your partner should immediately knock him off you. If you have no partner available or they're indisposed, be prepared to button-mash out of its attack.

enemies.name: Oko
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 6) These tiny flying insect-like B.O.W.s are completely harmless on their own. However, when they detect you with its radar-like senses, it will alert Ustanak to your location. It is possible to sneak up behind these and dispose of them using a stealth attack without being spotted.

enemies.name: Ubistvo
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 6) This humanoid B.O.W. has a chainsaw as an arm and is exceptionally deadly. In many stages, the Ubistvo cannot be killed and, as a result, must be avoided. Its chainsaw attack instantly kills you no matter how it hits you! Thankfully, Ubistvo's tactics are straightforward and easy to avoid.

enemies.name: Ustanak
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 6) This burly B.O.W. appears throughout Jake's campaign - like the classic Resident Evil enemy Nemesis - each time with a new tool of destruction attached to its arm. Many encounters with the Ustanak require that you simply run away or hide. But there are a few instances when you're forced to fight.

enemies.name: Haos
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 6) This enormous B.O.W. appears at the end of Chris' campaign and looks like an gigantic Rasklapanje but is vastly more lethal. This vicious monster is at times invincible and can only be damaged during specific stages. If he chases you, don't waste your ammunition, just focus on escaping.

enemies.name: Carla Radames
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 6) Carla mutates into a grotesque J'avo version that is practically invincible. When you first meet Carla, you have only one choice - escape. She spreads herself throughout the ship like an uncontrollable blob, blocking off corridors and spawning appendages to stop you escaping. She even has the ability to spawn copies of former self that will

enemies.name: Zombie
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 6) The original Resident Evil villain returns in its full, undead glory. The shambling undead generally try to get close and grab you. Some zombies carry melee and long-range weapons, but they are inaccurate and should be treated as any other zombie.

enemies.name: Bloodshot
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 6) Upon death, red-eyed zombies occasionally mutate into these grotesque B.O.W.s. The Bloodshot is a skinless, humanoid creature that is faster than normal zombies but difficult to take down.

enemies.name: Shrieker
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 6) These B.O.W.s are highly dangerous but not because of their offensive strength. They have a powerful scream that calls zombies to your location. If you see a Shrieker, take it out as soon as possible to prevent it summoning more enemies.

enemies.name: Whopper
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 6) This super-sized zombie isn't tricky or threatening but is durable and difficult to defeat. They require significant ammunition to take down and aren't easily thwarted by counter-attacks or martial arts.

enemies.name: Zombie Dog
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 6) After a long absence, this legendary Resident Evil mainstay returns, this time mutated from the C-Virus. These hounds of hell are easy to defeat, but are very quick and difficult to hit.

enemies.name: Brzak
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 6) This shark-like creature chases Leon and Helena through the underground of the Cathedral and is nearly impossible to kill. You can't fight the Brzak, you can only run from it. Therefore do not bother wasting any ammunition on it.

enemies.name: Ogroman
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 6) This giant B.O.W. roams the streets of Edonia, looking for BSAA agents to crush. Despite its size, Ogroman is rather easy to beat, as long as you keep your distance. It can only attack with fist swipes and foot stomps, each of which you can avoid by staying far away.

enemies.name: Deborah Harper
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 6) Helena's younger sister, under the effects of the C-Virus, acts as a mid-boss for Leon's campaign and Ada's campaign. Deborah's humanoid form is practically invincible and cannot be damaged. Instead, you must target the glowing spots on the tentacles that she sprouts when she attacks. Heavy weaponry isn't necessary as these shatter easily w

enemies.name: Derek Simmons
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 6) Mutated by the C-Virus, the National Security Advisor serves as the final boss of Leon's campaign and Ada's campaign. Like many J'avo , Simmon's has the ability to transform, although he can transform into several giant beasts, including a centaur and a Tyrannosaurus Rex, each with its own unique abilities.

weapons.text: Pipe Bomb (Resident Evil Village) A handmade pipe bomb. When thrown, it explodes violently upon impact or after a set amount of time. A weapon you can throw that will detonate and cause massive damage to nearby enemies. These explosives also have a practical use. You can use them to destroy cracked walls throughout various locations to access additional areas. These locations are listed as follows: Use one on the cracked wall behind the movable shelves inside Castle Dimitrescu's Armory in order to defeat Cassandra Dimitrescu . Use one on the cracked wall inside Castle Dimitrescu's Special Chambers to solve the puzzle in this room. Use one on the cracked wall in the south west corner of Heisenberg's Factory's Backup Generator Room in order to access a secret room with additional items. Use one on the cracked wall on the north side of Heisenberg's Factory's MB3 Maintenance Passage to access a hidden room with lots of valuables inside. These zombies are the poor residents of Wrenwood that were infected with a new mutated strain of the T-Virus by Victor Gideon . They will attack you with not only their bare hands, but anything they can get their hands on that could be used as a weapon.

However UV light is this monster's weakness, so entering a room with a light source will damage her and force her to retreat back into the darkness.

enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 4) El Gigante is a failed by-product of Los Illuminados' research. The rapid golem-like monster can barely distinguish friend from foe. The giant himself is invulnerable; you can only defeat him by killing the parasite on his back. You need to pelt El Gigante with shots until he holds his head in pain and drops to his knees, after which the pa

enemies.name: Colmillos
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 4) Los Illuminados misused wolves as guinea-pigs for their early Plaga experiments, with remarkable results from the point of view of the cult. The Colmillos have gone mad and pounce on anything that moves. If they sense danger, their backs spout tentacles, enabling them to execute an additional attack.

enemies.name: Bella Sisters
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 4) A much tougher variant of the normal Village Ganado , these hosts were not injected with an ordinary Plaga egg. Instead, their heads were made host to the parasite via the bloodstream, which is why they wear bandages over their faces. This method of infection has made them stronger and more resilient, and with the chainsaw they wield they a

enemies.name: Bitores Mendez
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 4) Bitores Mendez is the Pueblo village chief. Injected with a special Plaga, Mendez is endowed with extraordinary powers. As such, he is a dangerous opponent.

enemies.name: Castle Ganado
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 4) They act similar to the Village Ganados except fashioned in religious clothing and wielding deadlier weapons - which include maces, crossbows and scythes. Some even protect themselves from harm with full-height wooden shields, making dispatching of these zealots a much trickier affair.

enemies.name: Castle Ganado (Leader Zealot)
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 4) A variant of the Castle Ganado that wears a distinctive goat skull mask. These enemies are usually stronger than the standard Ganados, and sometimes carry a key item you need to progress through the game.

enemies.name: Garrador
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 4) The Garrador is a particularly strong Ganado, who carries an implanted, manipulated form of the parasite on his back. Immune to pain at all other spots, his body is vulnerable where it carries the Plaga. Hitting this spot makes the Garrador stagger; he can basically only be injured there. His eyes have been sewn shut during the painful oper

enemies.name: Armadura
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 4) Armaduras are an experimental project to grow Plagas without a living host - the suits of armour contain Plagas that mimic human movement. Therefore, their manoeuvres seem awkward and clumsy. If they take too much damage, the Plagas will emerge to defend their mechanical housing. In some Armaduras, the Plaga is not yet large enough to keep

enemies.name: Novistador
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 4) These are mere by-products of experiments conducted by Los Illuminados on humans and animals. These creatures avoid broad daylight, tending to stay in dark places. As a rule, Novistadors appear in swarms, so be watchful when you encounter your first specimen. There are tow types of Novistador - the strong one can turn invisible, while the w

enemies.name: Verdugo
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 4) Salazar's aide also acts as his bodyguard - for a reason. The skeletal monster can barely be vanquished by conventional means. Verdugo is about 20 times more resilient than a Ganado, moves with lightning speed and has a wide variety of attacks.

enemies.name: Ramon Salazar
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 4) Salazar, castellan of ancient lineage, is an adult despite his child-like stature. He is host to a mother parasite that is capable of producing new Plagas. He submits himself, along with his remaining aide, to a large Plagas structure, transforming into a mutant with ferocious attack power and deadly speed. You need to cause precise damage

enemies.name: Soldier Ganado
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 4) They act similar to the Village Ganados except fashioned in military gear and wielding deadlier weapons - which include stun rods, crossbows, maces and rocket launchers. Some even protect themselves from harm with full-height shields, making dispatching of these soldiers a much trickier affair.

enemies.name: Hammer Ganado
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 4) These are a larger variant of the Soldier Ganado . They do not carry projectile weapons, but instead choose to wield a large spiked hammer that causes a lot of damage if you get struck with it. In addition to this, these foes also wear metal body armor, making them a formidable enemy to take down. Aim for the head!

enemies.name: J.J.
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 4) A large Soldier Ganado that requires its immense strength to wield a personal Gatling Gun. He will only trigger his weapon when he has a direct line of sight of you, and since there's a slight pause between the weapon spinning up and it actually firing bullets, use this gap to unload your most powerful weapons into him.

enemies.name: U-3
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 4) U-3 is one more monstrous Los Illuminados guinea-pig. The experiment combining man and beast with the help of Las Plagas failed spectacularly. The deformed horror was banned from the earth's surface and now spends its miserable life guarding access to the sand fortress in the container cave.

enemies.name: Jack Krauser
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 4) Leon's former comrade, Jack Krauser , has armed himself with superhuman powers, allowing him to move at lightning speed and leap 20 metres into the air. During the main confrontation with him at the sand fortress, you see the full extent of his powers as he mutates his left arm into a wing-like weapon, capable of deflecting bullets.

enemies.name: Regenerator
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 4) These fearsome, highly developed species are the latest creations of the Los Illuminados experiments. Their superior metabolism is capable of regenerating lost body parts within seconds. Fortunately, the speed in which the monsters can move is far from satisfactory fro the cult. This is due to a lack of communication between the individual

enemies.name: Iron Maiden
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 4) Arguably even more gruesome than the Regenerator , the Iron Maiden is covered with spikes it can extend in no time at all. Rather than biting its victims, this monstrosity draws it close and rams it onto its spikes.

enemies.name: Osmund Saddler
enemies.intro: (Resident Evil 4) The leader of the Los Illuminados cult, Osmund Saddler , shows off his full power as he transforms into a four-legged abomination during the final chapter of Leon's adventure.
